lead: a hospital form asks for one next of kin and one contact, and filling it in truthfully is the first time in thirty years that both halves of your life have appeared on the same page.
sun: nothing was ever concealed. both directions are carried at their own weight, which uses the whole of a week and leaves no hour for describing one to the other, and the two sets of people have no occasion to meet. what each of them holds is accurate: the man who has known you since you were nineteen carries an account of you with a whole second life missing and no error in it anywhere.
moon: The Hideaway put a cover over the pair of them without anybody asking for one, and the whole of it stands on one item: no week of yours has ever been run by another person. nothing about the arrangement exists on paper anywhere somebody could reach. take a fortnight out of your hands and it goes public in an afternoon, to people who will read it as a lie.
pull: each end holds an accurate half and takes it for the whole. the only place the two are ever in the same room is inside you, and nothing was ever built to house that.
tension: the person you live with used the word secretive in the summer, and your oldest friend used it in the autumn, and neither knew the other had. each of them is standing inside one of the halves with everything they have ever asked for. what they cannot get to is the other half of a working life, and describing it to one end turns it, in the telling, into the thing they suspected.
cost: two lives ran at their own weight for thirty years, neither ever living on what the other could spare, and both sets of people had somebody entirely present for as long as they had you. none of it can be delegated for a single week. when it goes it goes at both ends on one afternoon, and each half learns what the other was from a stranger holding a list.

lead: whoever moves in here is handed two complete systems and no key to which one is running tonight. nothing indoors was ever reduced to a single method, both were built properly, and both are still in use.
sun: both methods went into the fabric at their proper size, and neither was ever named the house rule: two ways of settling a quarrel, two ways of carrying a debt, two ways of sitting with somebody who is dying. both are first answers. a household running two working methods for everything has never been stuck, and has no phrase in it for the way things are done here.
moon: the walls went up around the doubleness early, and the doubleness became the address, so the three who grew up in here have habits where other families have a rule. what makes the enclosure hold is that it has two sides, and nobody indoors has ever been asked to notice either. an occupant does not give an account of the room.
pull: the house has no single way of doing anything and has never yet failed to know what to do. the people raised inside that cannot say what they were raised inside.
tension: the phrase that arrives from outside is that nobody knows where they stand here, and it arrives from decent people — an in-law, a neighbour of twenty years — who cannot find the rule and assume there is a temper somewhere behind it. saying that both procedures are permanent and equally serious sounds, out loud, like a family being defended. so the second method gets given to visitors as a quirk, which is the only version anybody outside holds.
cost: nothing indoors has ever come apart over method, because a second working answer was in the room every time the first one failed, and people have lived through things here that empty other houses. the place runs on two people holding two systems at once. each of your children left with one, and each of their houses has a rule now, and one way through a bad year.

lead: she was four years later into it than everybody who started when she did, and she is the only one of them who can do the other side of the work as well.
sun: everybody you pick up gets walked along both roads from the start, in parallel, because handing somebody a single competence and calling them ready is, in your hands, sending them out half-made. so every passage you run takes about twice as long as the one running beside it, and the person being taken cannot tell which parts of it are the delay and which are the second road.
moon: you stop at the edge, the way you always have, except that you are now standing at the edge of two countries per person. what happens on the far side of either goes unreported: they write once, warmly, from a life you have never entered, and the letter names one of the roads because that is the one they are living on.
pull: they arrive carrying two roads, and inside five years each has quietly stopped using one, never the same one twice. what you taught exists whole in nobody.
tension: the people who send you their juniors say, kindly, that you hold them too long. the ones you took are no use as evidence: each tells the story of getting there with a single road in it, because the second road was never given a name while it was being walked. it was the extra work, the part that made everything slower. so the only witness to it is a person who cannot describe what was done to them.
cost: the ones you brought on survive the end of the thing they trained for. three have rebuilt a life on the road they had stopped using, and all three call that luck. what reaches you is a card at the new year, warm, from a country you have not entered, about a job you had no part in and cannot picture.

lead: nobody alive has stood beside this long enough to see it work. both directions have run without a gap since your twenties, and every judgement anybody has made about you was taken off a segment of that.
sun: neither direction shows a finish anywhere in the first thirty years, so a five-year view of you gives one thing done properly and another at an odd angle beside it. that view is accurate for its length, and its length is five years. what the two amount to appears only across the whole run, and nobody has been standing next to you for the whole run.
moon: a single unbroken length is what there is, no year of it separable from the rest, hauled at from both ends every season. the run offers no natural place to come in, so everybody came in partway and began counting there, which leaves each of them holding an exact reading of a decade and calling it a reading of you.
pull: the only person who has the whole length of it is you, and your own account is the one form of evidence that does not count anywhere.
tension: at every stage somebody has had a theory, and the theories are built off a decade each: at thirty you were spreading yourself, at forty you were avoiding a decision, at fifty-five you had settled for two half-lives. each was fair on what was in the room. the correction needs forty years produced at once, and nowhere gives a person forty years, so the current theory stands until the current people leave and the next lot start again.
cost: both directions are finished work by now, forty years each, which no short view of your life has ever contained. none of it can be demonstrated inside the time anybody gets with you. whoever could say what the run was would have had to arrive at the start and still be here, and the last one who qualified died in the winter.
